overview: White develops the king's knight to e2, keeping the f-pawn free for f4 and the knight flexible for g3, c3 or d4. After 2...Nf6 or 2...Nc6, White typically plays Nbc3, g3 and Bg2, or d4, aiming for a calm game with a King's Gambit-style f4 thrust held in reserve. Black can equalise with ...d5 or a solid ...Nc6 and ...Bc5.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Ne2 and Nbc3, then fianchetto with g3 and Bg2, or play f4 and d4 for a big centre.
Keep the king's knight flexible and delay committing the f-pawn.

black_ideas.idea: Strike the centre with ...d5 or develop ...Nc6, ...Bc5 and castle.
Exploit the slightly awkward knight on e2 by occupying the centre quickly.

typical_structures.structure: e4 against e5 with White's knight on e2 and a possible g3/Bg2 set-up.

character.notes: Quiet developing system with few forced tactics; neither side is pushed hard.

structure.notes: Centre stays undecided with e4/e5 and later d3 or d4 choices.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom play 2.Ne2 at all; it is rare and chosen for surprise.

level.notes: No heavy theory; plans are simple.

character.reason: Quiet but not especially solid or sharp.

structure.reason: Centre undecided; White can still choose f4, d4 or d3.

level.reason: Simple but unusual, not a standard coach pick.

plans.reason: g3 and Bg2 is the common set-up.
